mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with higher 20-day S&P 500 forward returns due to reduced discount rates and increased liquidity, leading to positive equity returns. The relationship is negative: lower FEDFUNDS implies positive returns.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns show no negative correlation with FEDFUNDS (Rank IC < 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window, or the t-test for the mean return difference between low and high FEDFUNDS quintiles is not significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in annual CPI inflation above 2.5% (CPIAUCSL) signals an inflationary environment that leads to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns due to anticipated central bank tightening and reduced risk appetite.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in periods where CPIAUCSL annual inflation rate > 2.5% are not significantly negative (mean return > -0.5% or t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous labor market slack (UNRATE > 5.0%) and declining industrial production (INDPRO < 100) signal an imminent economic contraction, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns due to heightened recession risk and reduced corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in periods meeting the trigger condition (UNRATE>5.0 and INDPRO<100) are not significantly negative (mean return > -0.5% or t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 3.0%), a rising unemployment rate (UNRATE > 5.5%) signals an imminent recession, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns due to reduced corporate earnings and increased risk aversion.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in periods meeting the trigger condition (FEDFUNDS>3.0 and UNRATE>5.5) are not significantly negative (mean return > -0.5% or t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 800,000 units, it signals weak consumer demand and potential economic slowdown, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in periods where HOUST < 800.0 are not significantly negative (mean return > -0.5% or t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 100) signals a supply shock or economic contraction, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns due to reduced corporate earnings and increased market volatility.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in periods where INDPRO < 100 are not significantly negative (mean return > -0.5% or t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.5% in a single month signals aggressive monetary tightening, leading to negative 5-day S&P 500 returns due to immediate market panic and reduced risk appetite.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns in periods where FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.5% in a single month are not significantly negative (mean return > -0.5% or t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1 < 15900 billion) signals an economic recession, leading to positive 60-day S&P 500 returns due to eventual central bank stimulus and market stabilization.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns in periods where GDPC1 < 15900.0 are not significantly positive (mean return < 0.5% or t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
